summary:
Post-discharge med reconciliation per RBC-TOC-02 for 3 patients, each with a progress note and an addendum.

WALTER KIM (pt-0005):
- Furosemide changed from 20 mg daily to 40 mg BID (mr-t0001), per the signed addendum doc-00009.
- KCl stopped (mr-00076), per the discharge summary.
- Omeprazole kept; pantoprazole was a formulary substitution and was not ordered.
- Metoprolol XL, atorvastatin, aspirin: no change.
- Lisinopril: first kept on hold because K was 5.4 on 10/21, and a task was created (task-t0003). A repeat BMP arrived 10/23 (K 4.7, SCr 1.21), so it was RESUMED (mr-00072). task-t0003 could not be cancelled; message comm-t0015 explains it is resolved.
- An unsigned draft addendum (furosemide 60 mg BID) was not acted on.

TERENCE STARK (pt-0004):
- Carvedilol was first raised to 12.5 mg BID per the discharge summary. A signed addendum then arrived that reverses it, so it was set back to 6.25 mg BID (mr-t0012).
- Aspirin and insulin 70/30: no change.
- FLAGGED: atorvastatin 80 fills cover about 24% of the 180 days before admission; order not changed (comm-t0006).
- FLAGGED: outside glipizide 5 mg from Dr. Desai has no clinic order and is not mentioned at discharge (comm-t0007).

EARNEST ROBERTS (pt-0044):
- Insulins and rosuvastatin: no change.
- Lisinopril 20 was resumed (SCr 1.08, K 4.6 on 10/22). A new K of 5.5 on 10/23 then arrived, so it was RE-HELD (mr-00373).
- FLAGGED: task-t0014, due 10/27, to recheck K and decide on lisinopril.

All 4 new inbox items were reviewed and completed.

evidence.quote: The outside pharmacy claims history (doc-00007) shows glipizide 5 mg tablets, #30 for 30 days, filled 07/30, 08/29 and 09/28/2026 at Lakeview Drug. The prescriber was Anil Desai, MD (Valley Endocrinology). There is no Riverbend order for it
so the fills cover about 44 of the 180 days before admission on 10/16 (about 24%, well under 80%)
